title: Mark Thornton: Higher Rates Are Coming — Gold & Silver Could Be the Winners
speaker: Mark Thornton (Mises Institute), interviewed by Daryl Thomas

macro_themes.view: Rates are in a secular uptrend since 2021 with possible spikes; long bonds no longer act as a shock absorber for stocks.
Fed is behind on its 2% target and quietly inflating; CPI (~3.5-4%) likely goes higher, aided by oil and food prices.
US equities are at record valuations driven by a handful of names; investors should reduce stock exposure.
Portfolios should shift to short-duration bonds/cash, gold, silver, commodities and oil, which are historically undervalued.
Dollar has stabilised/risen short term, but its long-run purchasing power and DXY value should decline.

calls.reason: Long-run inflation, falling dollar and bond bear market make gold a core holding; short-term dollar strength only hurts it in traders' minds.
calls.quote: what does that leave you with? Well, it leaves you with commodities. It leaves you with gold and silver

calls.reason: Same hard-money thesis as gold: inflation and debt monetisation favour silver over paper assets.
calls.quote: it leaves you with commodities. It leaves you with gold and silver uh and assets that are geared towards gold, silver

calls.reason: 40-year rate downtrend ended in 2021; deficits, ~$10T annual rollover and inflation push long rates higher, possibly in spikes.
calls.quote: we're in a longterm bare market in bonds. So that means we're looking at an upward trend in interest rates

calls.reason: Dollar stabilised over summer and is rising a little short term, but long-run trend in purchasing power and versus other currencies is down.
calls.quote: the long-term trend for the dollar looks to me like it's down

calls.reason: Market at its most overvalued in history, narrow leadership; investors should reduce stocks as higher rates pressure valuations.
calls.quote: investors and savers have got to look um to reduce stocks which are highly highly overvalued

calls.reason: Oil is historically undervalued and higher oil prices are baked in even if the Persian Gulf war is resolved.
calls.quote: with oil prices going higher and food prices going higher even if we could solve the war in the Persian Gulf. I think those trends …

notes: No date stated in transcript; listing says 19 minutes ago (2026-10-08). Bond view recorded as TNX (yields up); he also says long-bond prices will fall (TLT bearish equivalent). No price levels or targets given. Oil call is partly an inflation statement plus 'very undervalued' commodities remark.
